q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to an 8-month-old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Do not use ibuprofen in children younger than 6 months [6]. Know your child's weight before giving it, and give it every 6 to 8 hours [6]. Check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable, or speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [3]. Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the ibuprofen is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Give small sips of oral rehydration solution, which you can buy without a prescription, to replace the fluids and electrolytes lost through vomiting [5]. The SEUP advises waiting about 20 minutes after a vomit, then giving 2 to 5 ml of oral rehydration solution every 5 minutes for an hour, and increasing the frequency slowly if he keeps it down [3]. Do not use homemade solutions like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [3], and avoid sports drinks, which have too much sugar and the wrong electrolytes for a child [4]. Keep offering breast milk or dairy as normal if he wants it [4].

See a doctor if he is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds, if he vomits a lot or cannot keep down solids or liquids, if the vomit is green, bloody or looks like coffee grounds, or if he is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or passes little urine [7].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text: Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is to keep giving fluids [3][5]. Offer oral rehydration solution: after a vomit, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, and if it is well tolerated you can slowly increase how often you give it [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [5]. See your doctor if your child is very drowsy, vomits many times, or will not take fluids [3].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in asthma, according to the WHO, and it is often triggered by colds or by things like dust, smoke, pollen or strong smells [4]. In preschool children, viral respiratory infections are the main cause of this kind of cough and wheeze, according to the SEUP [1]. If your child has been diagnosed with asthma, the SEUP says treatment with salbutamol should be started, given through a spacer, never straight into the mouth [7].

See a doctor if your child is very restless or sleepy, turns blue or pale, is breathing faster and faster, or needs inhalations every two hours or less [7].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text: A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Whooping cough also starts like a cold, with a runny nose and mild, occasional cough that may last 1 to 2 weeks before the coughing fits begin [1]. Those fits come in spells, are often worse at night, and can last for several weeks or months [4]. In babies, the signs can be different: they may cough very little or not at all, pause in their breathing, or turn blue — get medical care right away if that happens [1]. See your doctor if the cough is getting worse, comes in bouts, or your child has trouble breathing [3][4].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough with no fever and a normal appetite is not, by itself, a sign that something is wrong. A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1]. Fever is not an illness; it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers are harmless and self-limiting, according to the AEPap [5].

See a doctor if he stops wanting to eat, is not his usual self, or seems dehydrated, such as nappies that are not very wet or no tears when crying [1].

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
Itchy raised bumps on the legs are common in small children, and hives is one of the usual causes [1]. Hives are raised, itchy patches or bumps that can vary in size and often come in groups [1]. For a young child, antihistamine treatment may help the itching, but it might not be suitable for young children, so ask a pharmacist or your doctor first [7]. Scratching can make skin redder and itchier, so keep nails short and the skin moisturised [4].

See a doctor if the rash comes with swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, fast or struggling breathing, a tight throat, or if your child becomes limp, floppy or hard to wake [7].

Spots that don't bother her and keep appearing each morning are common in nappy rash, which can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [2]. The spots may be red or brown, and can be harder to see on brown and black skin [2]. Nappy rash can also cause red or raw patches, scaly dry skin, or an itchy bottom [1][2].

See your doctor if the rash spreads, blisters, or she becomes uncomfortable or distressed [1][2].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries are not serious, according to the NHS [2]. After a blow to the head, the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1]. Watch him for the first 24 hours for warning signs [3].

Get urgent medical help if he was knocked out, cannot stay awake, has a seizure, is vomiting repeatedly, is confused or hard to wake, has clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears, or has trouble walking, speaking or understanding [2][4]. Also seek urgent care if the fall was from more than one metre [5].

He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. Rest from sport and screens for 24 to 48 hours, then return gradually [4]. Most children recover quickly [6].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text: Around 6 months, milk alone no longer covers a baby's energy and nutrient needs, so complementary foods are needed, according to the WHO [1]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and build up the consistency and variety of foods over time [1]. Give 2–3 meals a day at 6 to 8 months, and keep breastfeeding on demand alongside them [1]. Offer one new food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Do not give honey, cow's milk or unpasteurised foods before 12 months, and avoid choking hazards like whole nuts and grapes [5]. Ask your pediatrician if you have questions about starting solids or about peanut-containing foods [5].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and the AEP recommends keeping it on demand, at least two dairy servings a day (about 500 ml) [2]. Water is not given as a set amount: the AEP says the amount a baby eats or drinks is decided by the baby, so offer it and let them take what they want rather than aiming for a fixed quantity [6]. During illness, the WHO says to increase fluid intake, including more frequent breastfeeding [1]. If you are worried your baby is drinking too little or too much, or is unwell, speak to your doctor.

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for young children to refuse new foods at first, and repeated exposure to different flavours helps: the taste for sweet, salty, sour and bitter is formed early, and early exposure to different flavours may reduce the risk of refusing new foods, according to the AEP [3]. Offer the whole variety of fruits and vegetables progressively, at any daily meal, and vary how you present them — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [3]. There are no better fruits than others to start with; it depends on the family's tastes [3]. Keep offering vegetables alongside the fruit rather than replacing one with the other, and give whole fruit rather than juice, since juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods [3]. If your child is under one year, avoid green leafy vegetables such as chard, spinach or borage because of the risk of methaemoglobinaemia; if you do give them, they should be less than 20% of the plate, and up to age 3 no more than one daily portion of these vegetables [3].
sources: [3] AEP — "Recomendaciones de la AEP sobre la alimentación complementaria" (2018), section

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula should be a complement to solid food, not the main source of nutrition. The WHO recommends breastfeeding continue up to 2 years or beyond while nutritionally adequate and safe complementary foods are introduced from 6 months [1]. Complementary feeding means offering solid or liquid foods in addition to milk or formula, not as a replacement for it [2]. The first two years are especially important, since optimal nutrition during this period reduces illness and supports growth and development [3]. If your daughter is mostly on formula, it is worth talking to your doctor about how to build up her solid foods.

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby, and it is not essential for a baby to have a bowel movement every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is the consistency: constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, and sometimes fewer stools [6]. In a baby under 6 months, the usual feeding — breast milk or formula — is kept as it is [3]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of tummy pain, or repeated vomiting [3].

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text: Night waking at this age is common and usually normal: around 30% of children still wake at night by their first birthday, and between 20% and 40% of children under three do, according to the PUC Chile manual [2]. Waking every two hours is often a sleep-habit problem rather than a disease — if a baby always falls asleep in your arms, they will want the same conditions to fall back asleep when they wake [2]. The manual advises parents not to intervene too much, so the child learns to settle back to sleep on their own [2]. Night waking itself does not affect growth [4]. See your doctor if your baby also has fever, poor feeding, or seems unwell during the day.

text:
A cough that comes on when he lies down can be part of asthma-type symptoms: children may have a cough, sometimes at night, along with a feeling of breathlessness, according to the SEUP [4]. Preschool children most often get this kind of wheeze and cough from viral respiratory infections, and it can also be triggered by colds, allergy, pollution or exercise [3]. q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using a reliever inhaler more often than usual is one of the signs that the asthma is not fully controlled, and it is a reason to seek medical care [7]. Asthma cannot be cured, but it can be controlled with the right treatment, and the treatment depends on how frequent the symptoms are [2]. Reliever inhalers such as salbutamol open the airways and ease symptoms, while steroid inhalers reduce the inflammation behind them [2]. Always give the inhaler with a spacer, never straight into the mouth, because it works better that way [7].

See a doctor now if he is very agitated or drowsy, turns blue or pale, breathes faster and faster, or needs inhalations every two hours or less [7].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text: A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that causes noisy, high-pitched breathing and a barking cough, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold and the symptoms usually get worse at night, lasting three to five days [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home [3]. Watch for difficulty breathing — ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, fast breathing, or tiredness — and if that appears, she needs to be seen [1][4]. If you are worried about her breathing, contact your doctor promptly [3].

See a doctor if he has trouble breathing, is breathing fast, is tired when walking or running, or if his chest hurts when he breathes [2].

A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. They usually affect children between 6 months and 6 years old, and most last 2 to 3 minutes [2]. You cannot prevent febrile seizures [6].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text: A febrile seizure is not usually serious and is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. Children who have had one have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later in life, but this is rare [3]. They usually affect children between 6 months and 6 years old, so a child of 4 is still in that range [5]. If he ever has another seizure, keep him safe while you wait for help: check the time it starts and ends, protect his head, and move dangerous objects away [4].

q: my 7 year old says her neck hurts with a fever
text:
A fever is a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most causes are mild viral illnesses [3]. A stiff neck together with a fever is a warning sign that needs urgent medical attention [7]. Do not wait to see if it settles — take her to be seen straight away [7].

Watch for these too, and get help immediately if they appear [7]:

- A rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it
- Being bothered by light
- Unusually cold hands and feet, or blotchy, blue or grey skin
- Drowsiness that is hard to wake her from, or confusion
- Difficulty breathing

Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [7].

q: my child has a sore throat and white stuff on the tonsils
text:
A sore throat with white patches on the tonsils can be tonsillitis, an infection of the tonsils that is a common childhood illness, according to the NHS [1]. Children may also have a high temperature, problems swallowing, coughing, a headache, earache or feel sick [1]. Sore throats are usually caused by viruses, and they normally get better by themselves within a week [4][6].

To help soothe it, offer plenty of water and cool or soft foods, and let them rest [6]. Do not give young children anything small and hard to suck, because of the risk of choking [6].

See your doctor if the symptoms do not go away within a week, or if your child keeps getting throat infections [2]. Get medical help now if there are pus-filled spots on the tonsils, or a sore throat so painful it is difficult to eat or drink [2].

q: when should I take my kid to the doctor for a sore throat
text:
Sore throats are very common and usually nothing to worry about, and they normally get better by themselves within a week, according to the NHS [5]. They are usually caused by viruses like a cold or flu, and only very occasionally by bacteria [3]. For most children, treatment is rest, plenty of fluids, cool or soft foods, and paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain [5][6]. Children should not take aspirin [1].

See a doctor if your child is under 5 and needs help for a sore throat, or if it does not improve after a week [2]. Get urgent help if your child has difficulty breathing or cannot swallow, is drooling, or makes a high-pitched sound when breathing [2].

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible with a body thermometer — that reading is almost certainly 105 °F, which is about 40.5 °C (104.9 °F). Fever is not an illness in itself: it is a sign that the body is fighting an infection, and infections cause most fevers, according to MedlinePlus [1]. A child of this age has fever from 37.5 °C (99.5 °F) measured under the arm, and it is often due to a simple cold or other viral infection, according to the NHSRC [3]. Fever is a normal, good response and rarely goes above 40.5 °C (104.9 °F) on its own [5]. What matters is how your child looks and behaves, not the number alone.

See a doctor if your child is very sleepy, confused, irritable or behaving unusually, or has a severe headache or repeated vomiting [6].

Hard, dry poop that hurts to pass is constipation, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The main sign is stool that is harder and less frequent, sometimes with tummy pain or pain when passing it [2][4]. In most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

text:
Itchy red patches on the arms can have several common causes. Eczema causes dry, itchy skin and a rash, and scratching can make it redder and itchier, according to MedlinePlus [2]. It is not contagious and often runs in families alongside hay fever and asthma [2]. Scabies causes intense itching, often worse at night, with bumps and lines on the fingers, wrists and arms, according to the WHO [3]. Avoiding things that irritate the skin, such as certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, can help prevent some types of eczema [2].

See your doctor if the itching is intense, is worse at night, or the patches spread or do not improve.

q: my toddler is wheezing after running around outside
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Wheezing after running is a known pattern: symptoms can start after physical effort, according to the SEUP [7]. Wheezing is the whistling sound heard when air leaves the lungs, and it happens because the bronchi narrow [2][7]. In preschool children, the most common cause of wheezing is viral respiratory infections [2]. Not every child who wheezes will go on to have asthma [2].

See a doctor if your child has intense coughing, serious breathing problems, or pale or bluish colour in the face, lips and nails [4].

q: my 4 year old has earache after a cold
text:
An earache after a cold is often acute otitis media: infection and inflammation of the middle ear, behind the eardrum, which usually happens as a complication of an upper respiratory cold with a lot of nasal mucus, according to the SEUP [5]. It is one of the most common infections in young children [5].

Watch for signs that your child is getting worse: difficulty breathing (ribs showing or chest sinking in, fast breathing, tiring when walking or running) or chest pain when breathing [4]. Also seek care if their general condition worsens — they seem low, drowsy or very irritable — or if breathing becomes difficult [4].

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly
text:
A blocked nose and trouble feeding are common with a cold: sneezing, a blocked nose and runny mucus are usual symptoms, and they can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [3].

To help at home, the NHS suggests saline nose drops from a pharmacy for a blocked nose, and smaller feeds more often [1]. The SEUP also recommends washing the nose to keep it clear of mucus, feeding little and often, and holding your baby in a more upright position to make breathing easier [2]. Keep them away from tobacco smoke and wash your hands often [2].

See a doctor if your baby is having difficulty breathing — grunting, long pauses in breathing, or the tummy sucking in under the ribs [7].

q: my 2 year old has a temperature of 39.2 and cold hands
text:
A temperature of 39°C or higher in a child over 3 months is a reason to ask for an urgent appointment, according to the NHS [2]. Cold hands can go with a high temperature — a child who feels hot or cold to the touch, or is shivering, should also be checked [2].

Watch for breathing that is fast or difficult, ribs pulling in, or the chest sucking under, and for a child who is very tired, irritable or not themselves [2][5]. If any of these appear, seek care straight away [2].

Keep offering plenty to drink, and give the fever medicine your paediatrician usually recommends if they are uncomfortable [4].

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
Stomach ache and refusing food can go together with a tummy bug: norovirus causes vomiting, diarrhoea and tummy pain, and usually gets better in about 2 days, according to the NHS [4]. Constipation is another common cause — a child may have a stomach ache and feel sick if they have not pooed at least 3 times in the last week, or if their poo is hard, dry or lumpy [6].

Refusing food for a day or so is common and often not a worry on its own: it's normal for young children to refuse to eat sometimes, and what they eat over a week matters more than in a single day [3].

See a doctor if the stomach ache is severe or keeps getting worse, if they are not drinking, or if they are not themselves.

q: my 8 month old hasnt had a wet nappy since this morning
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more is a sign of dehydration in babies, and babies are more likely to get dehydrated because they have more diarrhoea and vomiting, according to MedlinePlus [3][5]. Keep offering fluids — oral rehydration solution is what replaces the water and salts lost through diarrhoea, and it is the most important thing to do, according to the WHO [4]. Offer it in small amounts often, and keep breastfeeding normally, or more often if your baby wants it, according to the SEUP [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses [7].

See a doctor today: if your baby is very thirsty, cries without tears, wees little or has sunken eyes, or is very irritable, drowsy or less responsive [7].

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children with a high temperature can be looked after at home [1][2]. Keep breastfeeding as normal, offer plenty of fluids, and check on your baby regularly, including during the night [1]. The temperature usually comes down over 1 to 4 days [1].

Because your baby is under 6 months, a fever of 38°C needs medical advice — the NHS advises getting urgent advice for any baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or higher, and for babies of 3 to 6 months with a temperature of 39°C or higher [7]. Do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months or under 5 kg, and never give aspirin to a child under 16 [7]. Paracetamol can be given to babies over 2 months if they are distressed, but check the packaging or ask a pharmacist or doctor, and the dose depends on your baby's weight [1][6].

q: my son fell from bed and vomited twice
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
Vomiting after a head injury means the child should be checked, according to the SEUP [1]. The medical team will examine him and decide whether any tests are needed, although in most cases they are not [1]. If the child is under three months old, or the fall was from more than one metre, this also means going to the emergency department [1].

While you travel, keep him with you and watch his behaviour and how alert he is [1].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Mosquito bites usually itch, and most insect bites are harmless, according to MedlinePlus [1]. To calm the itch, a zinc and calamine lotion with menthol, phenol or camphor can be applied, and a mild topical corticosteroid such as hydrocortisone can be used for short periods [5]. Insect repellents also relieve bites that are already there [5].

See a doctor if the bites become infected or cause a serious allergic reaction [2].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A night-time cough in a 3-year-old can have several causes, and the organisations describe them differently. A cough that comes in bouts and is worse at night, sometimes with a "whoop" sound, is how the NHS describes whooping cough [2], and MedlinePlus says the coughing fits of whooping cough get worse and happen more often at night [1]. A barking cough like a seal, often worse at night, points to croup, according to the NHS [3]. Coughing mainly at night or early morning is also listed by MedlinePlus as a symptom of asthma in children [4].

None of these pages mentions a nebulizer, so whether to use one is not something they answer. Ask your doctor or pharmacist before giving any medicine, and see your doctor if your child is getting worse or not getting better [3].

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दानों के कई कारण हो सकते हैं। खसरा आमतौर पर ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षणों से शुरू होता है और कुछ दिन बाद दाने निकलते हैं; दाने पहले चेहरे पर बालों की लाइन पर सपाट लाल चकत्तों के रूप में आते हैं और फिर नीचे की ओर फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है [4]। चिकनपॉक्स में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और दानों से पहले या बाद में बुखार, दर्द और भूख में कमी हो सकती है [5]। हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथों-पैरों पर उभरे दाने आते हैं [3]। अगर दाने खुजली वाले उभरे चकत्ते लगते हैं, तो वह एलर्जी (पित्ती) हो सकती है, जिसका इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर हो सकता है [6]।

दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें। अगर मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या बच्चे को साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, तो तुरंत मदद लें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ में पॉटी करते समय बच्चे का रोना आम बात है — रोने के सामान्य कारणों में कब्ज़ भी शामिल है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]। अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे शांत या ध्यान भटका नहीं पा रहे हैं, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है [4]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें या अपने इलाके की मेडिकल हेल्पलाइन पर कॉल करें अगर बच्चा बीमार लगे, जैसे तेज़ बुखार हो या दूध पीने में दिलचस्पी न हो [4]। तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें अगर बच्चा दौरा पड़े, त्वचा या होंठ नीले-भूरे-पीले पड़ जाएँ, बेहोश या ढीला हो, साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, या पिछले 8 घंटे में पेशाब न हुआ हो [4]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे का ठंड लगना, कंपकंपी आना और हाथ-पैर ठंडे तथा त्वचा पर जाल जैसा धब्बेदार रंग (कटिस मार्मोराटा) दिखना सामान्य है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [2]। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल पड़ जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है [2]।

बुखार का मतलब है शरीर का तापमान 38°C से ऊपर होना; यह शरीर के बचाव का संकेत है और अपने आप में गंभीरता का पर्याय नहीं है [4]। ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसका कारण साधारण, विशेषकर वायरल, संक्रमण होता है [4]।

अगर बुखार के साथ बच्चा बहुत सुस्त लगे, पानी न पी पाए या हालत बिगड़ती दिखे, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा

text: बच्चे का सुस्त हो जाना और ज़्यादा देर जागते न रहना गंभीरता के संकेत हैं, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार — ऐसे लक्षण दिखते ही तुरंत चिकित्सकीय सहायता लेनी चाहिए [2]। साँस लेते समय पसलियों का अंदर खिंचना, सीने से कराहने जैसी आवाज़, या त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून और चेहरे पर नीली झलक भी खतरे के लक्षण हैं [2]। अस्पताल जाते समय बच्चे को खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नमस्ते। बच्चे का कम पेशाब करना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऊपर दिए गए निर्देश के अनुसार आज ही डॉक्टर से मिलना ज़रूरी है।

SEUP के अनुसार, बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — सामान्य भोजन जारी रखें, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, ताकि उल्टी का ख़तरा कम हो [1]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाइयाँ और जूस से बचें; दूध और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, या बच्चा माँगे तो और भी बार-बार दें [1]। स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें, क्योंकि उनमें चीनी बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [1]।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, तरल या ठोस कुछ भी न रख पाए, या उल्टी हरी, ख़ून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो [1]।

banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसे उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

तेज़ बुखार के साथ त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तो तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए — यह SEUP के अनुसार आपातकालीन विभाग में दिखाने का संकेत है [1]। NHS के अनुसार बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, और यह आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। बच्चे को ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े न उतारें और न स्पंज करें, न ही ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाइयों में लपेटें [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें [2]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text: Paracetamol bukhar aur dard mein madad karta hai, aur aap ise dawai ki dukaan se le sakte hain [4]. q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi hona asthma ya crisis asmática ka lakshan ho sakta hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ki khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [1]. SEUP kehti hai ki bachchon ko khansi (kabhi raat ko), saans ki kami aur ghabrahat ho sakti hai, aur saans lete waqt seeti ki awaaz (sibilancias) sunai de sakti hai [3].

In bachchon ko doctor ko dikhana chahiye agar:
- seene mein dhadkan ya pasliyan saans lete waqt andar dhas rahi dikhein [3]
- honton ke aas-paas neela rang dikhe [3]
- bolne mein dikkat ho ya khansi lagatar rahe [3]

Agar yeh lakshan hain to turant medical madad lein [1].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ke lakshan ho sakte hain — chhote, ubhre hue dane aur khujli wali feeling iske aam lakshan hain, NHS ke mutabik [4]. Heat rash aam taur par apne aap kuch dinon mein theek ho jata hai [6]. Ise thanda rakhna sabse zaroori hai: dheele cotton kapde pehnaayein, halka bistar use karein, aur thande paani se nahiyein [4]. Khujli ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya ice pack, towel mein lipta hua) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur khujlane ke bajaye dane par thap-thap karein [4]. Perfume wale shower gel ya cream use na karein [4].

Doctor se milein agar dane zyada fail rahe hain, bukhar ho, ya aapko yakeen na ho ki yeh heat rash hai [6].
sources: [4] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of heat rash", p. 1 —

banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
तेज़ सांस लेना ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या RSV जैसी सांस की बीमारी का लक्षण हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में बच्चा तेज़ सांस लेता है, सांस में सीटी जैसी आवाज़ आती है, और दूध या खाना पीना कम कर देता है [3]। CDC कहता है कि RSV शुरू में हल्का लग सकता है, पर कुछ दिनों में गंभीर हो सकता है, और शुरुआती लक्षणों में नाक बहना, कम खाना-पीना और खांसी शामिल हैं, जो आगे चलकर सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ बन सकती है [2]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को सीधा और आराम से रखें, थोड़ा-थोड़ा करके तरल दें, और उसकी सांस और चेतना पर नज़र रखें [3][4]। अगर बच्चा दूध या पानी पीना बंद कर दे, बहुत सुस्त या चिड़चिड़ा हो जाए, या 12 घंटे से ज़्यादा पेशाब न करे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [3]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is a common pattern in whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, children get coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night, according to the NHS [2]. The cough may last for several weeks or months [2]. MedlinePlus describes the same thing: the coughing fits get worse and happen more often, especially at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more [3]. Croup is another cause of a night-time cough — a barking cough that sounds like a seal, often worse at night [5].

See a doctor if the cough is very bad and getting worse, or if your child is finding it hard to breathe properly [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text: A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by several different illnesses, and only a doctor can tell which one it is. Measles causes a red rash that usually starts on the head and moves down the body, along with fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Chickenpox also causes a widespread itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face and chest, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Measles can lead to serious problems, so see your doctor to have your child checked [2][4].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text: Not eating for two days is a warning sign that needs medical review, according to the SEUP [1]. The same guidance lists refusing to eat or drink, marked irritability or drowsiness, and persistent or intense tummy pain as reasons to seek care [1]. If your child is vomiting a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, that also needs review [3]. While you wait to be seen, keep offering small, frequent amounts of oral rehydration solution rather than home-made solutions or soft drinks [1]. Do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without checking with your doctor [1].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text: A whistling or wheezing noise with a congested chest in a 6-month-old can be a sign of bronchiolitis, which often starts like a cold with a cough and a blocked nose, according to the SEUP [5]. Breathing may become faster, feeding may get harder, and you may hear chest noises or see the ribs pull in [5]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better within about 3 weeks, according to the NHS [3]. Keep feeding your baby little and often, and watch their breathing and how they feed [3].

text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में खुद उतर जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]। बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — स्तनपान कराने वाली माँ सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें — और निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है, पर पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि वह इस उम्र के लिए ठीक है [3]। 6 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, और 16 साल से कम उम्र में एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाना या उसका शरीर गीले कपड़े से पोंछना नहीं चाहिए — तेज़ बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में भी न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ सकते हैं, सिर्फ माथा नहीं — यह भारत स्वास्थ्य की सलाह है [3]। बच्चे का खाना-पानी चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [3]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा है, बुखार 5 दिन या उससे ज़्यादा रहता है, या बच्चा खाने में रुचि न ले और सामान्य न लगे [7]।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text: सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी जैसी आवाज़ ब्रोन्कियल नलियों में रुकावट से होती है, और यह सल्ब्यूटामोल जैसी ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं से ठीक हो जाती है, SEUP के अनुसार [2]। छोटे बच्चों में ऐसी सीटी की आवाज़ का सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल बीमारियाँ हैं [2]। हर बच्चा जिसे बचपन में सीटी की आवाज़ आती है, बड़े होकर अस्थमा का मरीज़ नहीं बनता [2]। जिन बच्चों को एलर्जी है, जिनके माता-पिता को अस्थमा है या जिन्हें अंडे से एलर्जी है, उनमें अस्थमा होने की संभावना अधिक होती है [2]। अस्थमा के लक्षणों में खांसी, सीटी की आवाज़, सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ और छाती में जकड़न शामिल हैं, और ये हल्के या गंभीर हो सकते हैं, WHO के अनुसार [5]। अस्थमा के लक्षण दिखने पर स्वास्थ्य कर्मी से मिलना चाहिए [5]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई कारणों से हो सकते हैं। बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे दाने छोटे कीड़ों (स्केबीज़) से हो सकते हैं, जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं; ये अक्सर पहले उंगलियों के बीच दिखते हैं और आमतौर पर घर पर ही इलाज हो सकते हैं [4]। स्केबीज़ एक परजीवी संक्रमण है जो तेज़ खुजली और दाने पैदा करता है, और यह त्वचा के सीधे संपर्क से फैलता है [2]। इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवाओं से होता है [2]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो, घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो, त्वचा में संक्रमण लगे, या फ़ार्मेसी का इलाज करने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित मानी जाती है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के हल्के दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, लेकिन ये सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का इलाज आसानी से हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर कर रही है [6]। nidirect के अनुसार टीके सुरक्षित और प्रभावी हैं तथा गंभीर बीमारियों से बचाते हैं [4]।

भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है, इसलिए अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण की जानकारी अपने डॉक्टर से लें [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
3 saal ke bachche mein raat ki khansi asthma ka lakshan ho sakti hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik asthma ke symptoms mein khaas taur par raat ya subah jaldi khansi shamil hai [5]. SEUP ke mutabik asthma crisis mein bachche ko khansi (kabhi raat ko), saans ki kami aur ghabrahat ho sakti hai [1]. Agar saans tez ho, pasliyan ya seene ka nichla hissa andar dhase, ya seeti ki awaaz aaye, to doctor se milna zaroori hai [1]. Laringitis mein bhi bachche raat ko kaafi khansate hain aur theek se sote nahi [6].

Doctor se turant milein agar bachcha bahut bechain ya sust ho, rang neela ya peela pade, ya saans lene mein dikkat badhe [7].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche par red rashes ke baare mein: sarna (scabies) mein tez khujli hoti hai, khaas kar raat mein, aur chhote bachchon mein haath ki hatheli, pair ke talve aur sar ki twacha par zyada gadbad hoti hai, jismein dane (papules) aur line jaise nishan hote hain — yeh WHO kehta hai [2]. Sarna chhune se failti hai aur iska ilaaj cream ya dawa se hota hai [5]. Agar rashes ke saath tez bukhar, khansi, naak behna aur aankhein laal hon, to yeh khasra (measles) ho sakta hai, jismein daane pehle chehre aur gale par aate hain aur phir poore sharir par phailte hain — yeh bhi WHO kehta hai [3]. Khasra se bachav ka sabse achha tareeka vaccination hai [4].

Doctor se turant milein agar saans lene mein dikkat ho, honth ya gala soojh jaye, ya bachcha sust ya behosh jaisa lage [7].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text: Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai — polio ke khilaf teekakaran hi is bimari se bachav ka sabse asardar tareeka hai [6]. WHO ke mutabik sabhi bachchon ko polio se bachne ke liye teekakaran ka poora course milna chahiye [6]. Spain ke Ministry of Sanidad ke teekakaran calendar mein polio (VPI) ki dose 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein di jaati hai [3]. q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea after a trip is usually an infection of the gut, and the main risk is dehydration, according to the WHO [6]. Treatment includes oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or soft drinks to replace the losses [3].

See a doctor if there is blood in the stool, persistent diarrhoea, or signs of dehydration such as much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes, marked irritability or drowsiness [1][3].

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का इंजेक्शन लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव सामान्य हैं, चिंता की बात नहीं [5]। खसरे के टीके के 6-7 दिनों बाद भी हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं, जो अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]। आमतौर पर ये लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

अगर लक्षण ठीक न हों, या इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए, तो स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी से परामर्श करें [5]। बुखार की दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Dizziness after sun exposure is one of the symptoms of heat stroke, a serious condition that happens when the body cannot regulate its temperature, according to the SEUP [1]. Other signs to watch for are hot, red, dry skin, fever above 39°C, intense headache, nausea or vomiting, and confusion [1].

While waiting to be seen, move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, apply cool wet cloths to the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan [6]. Do not give fever medicines for heat stroke — physical cooling measures are used instead, according to the AEPap [5].

Get medical help right away if there is confusion, trouble speaking or moving, loss of consciousness, or persistent vomiting [7].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare

text:
Stomach ache is a common symptom in children and most causes are mild and get better on their own, such as constipation, gas or a tummy bug, according to the SEUP [2]. Constipation often causes stomach ache and bloating, and it is likely if your child has not pooed at least 3 times in the last week, or the poo is large, dry, hard or lumpy, or they strain or feel pain when they go [1].

For a 5-year-old, the main things that help are more fluids, especially water, and more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables — rather than juices, which have little fibre [3]. Most cases of childhood constipation are not caused by any disease, and laxatives or enemas should not be given without asking your doctor [3].

See a doctor if the pain is severe, if your child is very unwell and complaining a lot, if there is blood in the poo, or if they vomit repeatedly and cannot keep down food or drink [3].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text: Malaria and teething are told apart by what comes with the fever, not by the fever itself. In malaria the most common early symptoms are fever, headache and chills, and the first symptoms may be mild and similar to many other illnesses, so it can be hard to recognise, according to the WHO [1]. Malaria is a life-threatening disease spread by the bite of certain mosquitoes, mostly in tropical countries, and it does not spread from person to person [1]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1]. If your child has a fever and has been in a tropical area, get them seen by your doctor the same day — untreated falciparum malaria can become severe within 24 hours [1].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: At around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are needed alongside it, according to the WHO [3]. Start with small amounts — just a few pieces or teaspoons — and increase gradually as your baby grows [3]. Offer food before the usual milk feed, when your baby is not too tired and not too hungry, and let them set the pace [1]. Keep offering different foods even if they are refused; it can take 10 tries or more before a new food is accepted [1]. Breast milk or first infant formula stays the main drink in the first year, and you can offer sips of water from an open cup with meals [1]. Aim for 2–3 meals a day at this age [3].

text:
Watery stools with weakness can be gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious but can sometimes lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The WHO says diarrhoea should be treated with oral rehydration salts — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and that zinc supplements reduce how long the episode lasts and how much stool is passed [1]. text:
For diarrhoea, the main treatment is oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, according to the WHO [1]. Most head injuries in children are not serious, according to the NHS [2]. The usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1]. Watch your child for the first 24 hours after the blow for warning signs [3].

See a doctor if there is intense or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion or disorientation, behaviour changes, trouble speaking or walking, or blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [4]. Go to the emergency department if your child is under three months old or fell from more than one metre [5].

Your child can sleep, but after a more significant blow it is advisable to wake them every 4 hours [6].

For an older child, dengue is a viral infection spread by mosquito bites, and most children get better in one to two weeks [1]. The common signs are high fever, headache, body aches, nausea and a rash, and there is no specific treatment — pain is managed, and the dose of any medicine depends on your child's age and weight [1]. Watch closely once the fever drops, because the warning signs of severe dengue often appear then: severe tummy pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums or nose, rapid breathing, restlessness or cold, pale skin [2]. q: my 1 year old baby skin has red spots with water inside
text:
Red spots with fluid inside them can be the first stage of the chickenpox rash, according to the NHS. The spots can be anywhere on the body, including inside the mouth and around the genitals, and they may be red, pink or darker depending on your child's skin tone [3]. They often start as raised spots that form a round or oval blister in the centre [3].

Spots with fluid can also be blisters from hand, foot and mouth disease, which look like they have fluid in them and usually appear on the hands and feet [6].

See your doctor if you are not sure what the rash is, or if your child seems unwell.

q: when to start feeding puree to 6 months old
text: From around 6 months of age you can start introducing solid foods, beginning with puréed or blended foods and moving on to mashed, lumpy or finger foods as soon as your baby can manage them, according to the NHS [2]. Some babies prefer to start straight away with mashed, lumpy or finger foods, while others need a little longer with smooth textures — either way is fine, and there is no right or wrong way [1][2]. Keep offering lumpy textures and your baby will get used to them [2]. If you have any concerns about how feeding is going, speak to your doctor.

q: is 6 in 1 vaccine safe for my baby
text:
There is no evidence that vaccine ingredients are harmful in the very small amounts used, according to the NHS [1]. Aluminium salts, the most common adjuvant, have been used safely in routine infant vaccines for more than 70 years, and no harmful effects have been seen with vaccines containing them [1]. Serious allergic reactions are rare and usually happen within minutes, when the person vaccinating your baby is trained to treat them immediately [7].

Speak to your doctor or nurse if you are worried about your baby having a vaccine or are not sure whether they can have it [7].

text: Not drinking and passing very little urine are signs of dehydration, and a child who is not drinking needs to be seen [3][6]. Do not use homemade solutions, fizzy drinks or sports drinks to replace the losses from diarrhoea or vomiting [6]. Keep breastfeeding normally, and more often if your child wants it [1]. If your child becomes drowsy, floppy or difficult to wake, that is a sign of severe dehydration and needs help straight away [5][6].

q: my 3 year old has severe chest congestion and flu
text:
A chest infection is an infection of the lungs or large airways, and it often follows a cold or flu [1]. The main signs are a chesty cough, sometimes with green or yellow mucus, wheezing, shortness of breath, chest pain, a high temperature, headache, aching muscles and tiredness [1]. These symptoms are unpleasant but usually get better on their own in about 7 to 10 days, though the cough and mucus can last up to 3 weeks [1].

Flu symptoms usually start suddenly and include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue, according to the WHO [3]. Most people recover on their own within a week by resting and drinking plenty of fluids [3]. People with other medical problems or severe symptoms should seek medical care [3].

See a doctor if your child is breathing fast or working hard to breathe, is struggling to feed, or looks pale or unwell [5].

q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby
text: At around 6 months, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to eating, according to the NHS [3]. They still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [3]. You can offer purées, mashed foods, cereals and soft finger foods, and let them feed themselves if they prefer — there is no right or wrong way, and self-feeding is no more likely to cause choking than spoon-feeding [1][2]. Introduce a cup at around 6 months and offer sips of water with meals [4]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your doctor when to start [3].

text:
Vomiting and loose stools like this are usually caused by a stomach bug, according to the NHS [1]. It is usually not serious, but babies can get dehydrated, so watch for the warning signs [3].

Keep feeding your baby: continue breastfeeding normally, and offer smaller amounts more often [5]. Oral rehydration solution is the main treatment [4]. Avoid fruit juice, fizzy drinks and sports drinks, and do not water down formula [5][6].

See a doctor if your baby is under 3 months and has vomited twice or more, is drowsy or floppy, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, has few or no wet nappies, or vomits green or bloody liquid [2][3].

q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol

Yes, paracetamol (Calpol) can help when a child is distressed or uncomfortable because of a fever, according to the NHS [3]. It also relieves pain from things like teething, earache and colds [3]. Paracetamol and ibuprofen are the medicines most used, given at the dose your paediatrician recommends every 6 to 8 hours [2]. q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and says diarrhoea should be treated with ORS, a solution of clean water, sugar and salt [1][6]. The WHO also lists zinc supplements as a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and are linked to a 30% reduction in stool volume [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. See a doctor for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1].

text: Los síntomas más habituales de un golpe en la cabeza son dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria transitoria, mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia, según la SEUP [1]. Es importante vigilar a la niña durante las primeras 24 horas tras el golpe para detectar síntomas de gravedad [2]. En casa hay que vigilar dolor de cabeza intenso o que no mejora con paracetamol o ibuprofeno, vómitos repetidos, desorientación o confusión, irritabilidad o dificultad para despertarla, cambios de comportamiento, dificultad para hablar o caminar, y salida de sangre o líquido claro por la nariz o los oídos [6]. También debe consultarse en urgencias si tiene un comportamiento o actitud que le preocupe [3]. Durante 24 a 48 horas se recomienda reposo físico y mental, sin deporte ni pantallas, y luego reincorporación gradual [6].

En niños mayores, la vacunación puede empeorar de forma transitoria su estado clínico, según el CAV-AEP [1]. La fiebre después de vacunarse es una reacción esperable y suele ser breve.

No puedo darte una dosis concreta de paracetamol o ibuprofeno: depende de la edad y el peso de tu hijo. Consulta la dosis con tu pediatra o en el prospecto.

Si la fiebre es alta, dura más de 48-72 horas o el niño está decaído, irritable o con mal aspecto, acude a tu médico.

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: mi hijo tiene 5 años y pesa 12 kilos, es normal?
text:
Según los patrones de crecimiento de la OMS (niño, 5 años):
• Peso para la edad: 12 kg → percentil 0.1 (z −3.22), bajo peso grave (por debajo de −3 DE).
⚠️ El peso está muy por debajo de lo que la OMS espera para esta talla o edad. Consulta con un médico pronto.
Dime también la talla y calculo el peso para la talla.
Un solo dato dice poco: lo que importa es la curva a lo largo del tiempo, y esa la tiene tu pediatra.

q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text: La erupción de los dientes de leche empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, con los incisivos centrales inferiores, según el Manual de Pediatría de la PUC Chile [6]. Que a los 9 meses todavía no le haya salido ninguno puede entrar dentro de la variación normal de cada bebé, así que no hay que alarmarse por ahora [6]. Mientras tanto, puedes revisarle la boca con calma: encías, lengua y mejillas, buscando inflamación o heridas [6]. Si te preocupa, coméntalo en la próxima revisión con tu pediatra o con un dentista infantil.

q: mi hija ha dejado de decir palabras que antes decía
text: Perder palabras que antes decía es una señal para actuar pronto: si tu hija ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía, conviene hablar con su pediatra y pedir una evaluación del desarrollo, según los CDC [3]. No esperes a que cumpla más edad ni a la próxima revisión [3]. Cuanto antes se empiezan los servicios de desarrollo, mejor es el resultado; entre ellos están la logopedia, la fisioterapia y la escuela infantil de desarrollo [5]. En España, la evaluación y la atención temprana se gestionan a través de tu pediatra y del centro de salud, que os derivarán al servicio correspondiente de vuestra comunidad [5].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text:
El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas distintas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no se debe a un problema del corazón [1]. Un dolor que aparece después de hacer ejercicio y mejora con el reposo puede deberse a una distensión o sobrecarga muscular [1]. También puede sentirse presión o dolor en el pecho por ansiedad, según la SEUP [3].

Conviene que lo vea un médico si el dolor va y viene, o si desaparece rápido pero sigue preocupando [7].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Desmayo haciendo ejercicio, o con palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho: que lo vean en urgencias hoy
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, según la SEUP [1]. Suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, y el calor extremo, el dolor, el miedo o el esfuerzo lo favorecen [1]. Antes de perder el conocimiento puede haber náuseas, visión borrosa, sudoración o zumbidos, señales que ayudan a reconocerlo y evitarlo la próxima vez [2]. Después de un rato de reposo, los niños suelen recuperarse en un par de minutos [5].

Si vuelve a sentirse mal, que se siente o se tumbe de inmediato, y si pierde el conocimiento, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado [5]. Conviene que beba más líquidos, sobre todo cuando hace ejercicio [4].

q: mi bebe esta vomitando y no consigue quedarse con ni siquiera pequeños sorbos
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Vomita TODO lo que toma y no retiene nada: es signo de peligro, hay que verlo hoy
text: Los vómitos son un síntoma de la gastroenteritis, que no suele ser grave, pero en los bebés el riesgo de deshidratación es mayor, según MedlinePlus [3][6]. Si no consigue retener líquidos, puede intentar darle pequeños sorbos de agua o trozos de hielo para chupar [2]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación ofreciendo soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas, en cantidades pequeñas y frecuentes, según la SEUP [5]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos, y no le des medicamentos para los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [5]. Mantén la lactancia materna normal o incluso más frecuente si el bebé la pide [4]. Consulta de nuevo si tiene mucha sed, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco o tiene los ojos hundidos [5].

q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text: La fruta y la verdura se pueden empezar a ofrecer en torno a los 6 meses, cuando la leche ya no cubre por sí sola las necesidades del bebé, según la OMS [2]. La AEP recomienda ir introduciendo toda la variedad disponible, en cualquiera de las comidas del día y variando la presentación: triturada, chafada o en trozos pequeños [1]. No hay frutas mejores que otras para empezar; la elección depende de los gustos de la familia [1]. Conviene introducir los alimentos de uno en uno, con unos días de intervalo, para ver cómo los tolera [4]. Durante el primer año, evita las verduras de hoja verde con muchos nitratos, como acelga, espinaca o borraja [1]. Mejor fruta entera que zumo: el zumo no aporta ventajas y aumenta el riesgo de caries [1].

q: mi hijo es asmatico y se le hunden las costillas al respirar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text: El hundimiento del pecho y las costillas al respirar es un signo de dificultad respiratoria que aparece en las crisis asmáticas, según la SEUP [4]. En una crisis asmática se administran de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol, de una en una, con cámara espaciadora (y mascarilla facial en los niños pequeños), y se repite esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Si la crisis no cede con el tratamiento en casa, hay que acudir lo antes posible a un centro sanitario, sin olvidar la cámara espaciadora [6]. Si el niño toma tratamiento de mantenimiento, debe seguir con él durante la crisis [6]. La mayoría de los broncoespasmos son leves y se resuelven en pocos días, aunque pueden durar hasta una semana [5].

text: De 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol (Ventolín), aplicadas de una en una con cámara espaciadora y mascarilla facial si es pequeño, según la SEUP [5]. Esa dosis se repite a los 10-15 minutos [5]. q: cuanto apiretal le toca a mi hijo de 12 kilos
text:
Paracetamol para 12 kg:
• Dosis: 180 mg cada 4–6 h (máx. 4 dosis/día).
  – Apiretal, gotas 100 mg/ml: 1.8 ml
  – jarabe 120 mg/5 ml: 7.5 ml
  – jarabe 125 mg/5 ml: 7.2 ml
  – jarabe 150 mg/5 ml (3 %): 6 ml
  – jarabe 160 mg/5 ml: 5.6 ml
  – jarabe 200 mg/5 ml (4 %): 4.5 ml
  – jarabe 250 mg/5 ml: 3.6 ml
  – gotas 100 mg/5 ml: 9 ml
  – gotas 200 mg/ml: 0.9 ml
La guía admite de 120 a 180 mg; esta es la dosis habitual para la fiebre.
Fuente: AEPap — Guía rápida de dosificación práctica en pediatría (3.ª ed.), tabla analgésicos/antitérmicos.
Comprueba siempre la concentración del envase. Si tiene menos de 3 meses, consulta antes de dar nada.

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text: Sí, se puede dar ibuprofeno (Dalsy) si el paracetamol no mejora la fiebre o el malestar, según la AEPap [6]. Lo razonable es esperar 3-4 horas desde el antitérmico y, si la temperatura sigue alta y el niño sigue incómodo, cambiar al ibuprofeno en la siguiente toma [6]. La SEUP recuerda que la fiebre puede persistir tras un antitérmico y que eso no significa que sea más grave [3]. La dosis de ibuprofeno depende del peso del niño; consúltala con su pediatra o en el prospecto [6].
sources: [3] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁL ES LA EVOLUCIÓN ESPERA

Mientras lo llevan, seguid ofreciéndole líquidos a menudo y en pequeñas cantidades, sin forzarle, y mantened la lactancia o el biberón con normalidad [2]. Si toma bien los líquidos, podéis ofrecerle también comida en pequeñas cantidades y con más frecuencia de lo habitual [1]. No le deis bebidas deportivas ni zumos, porque llevan demasiado azúcar [1].

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text:
La gastroenteritis suele mejorar por sí sola, con reposo y abundantes líquidos y electrolitos, según MedlinePlus [5]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación, y para eso las soluciones de rehidratación oral se ofrecen en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, según la SEUP [3]. No use soluciones caseras ni refrescos para reponer las pérdidas, ni le dé medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [2].

Consulte a su pediatra si el niño rechaza comer o beber, tiene mucha sed, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco o tiene los ojos hundidos, o si las deposiciones son muy líquidas y frecuentes y no logra beber al mismo ritmo que pierde [2].

q: mi hijo tiene manchas despues de tener fiebre, puede ser por la fiebre?
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico ese mismo día.

En un niño mayor, las manchas rojas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas son un signo de alarma: hay que consultar en urgencias, según la SEUP [2]. Lo mismo ocurre si aparecen manchas de forma súbita junto con hinchazón de labios o párpados, o si el niño está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable [2][6]. La fiebre en sí puede durar entre 2 y 4 días, y que no baje del todo con un antitérmico es frecuente y no indica por sí solo más gravedad [1].

Conviene vigilar su estado general y su color, y revisar si las manchas se aclaran al apretarlas [1]. Si no se aclaran, o si el niño empeora, acuda a urgencias [2].

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: mi hijo tiene 2 años y 39 de fiebre desde ayer, le doy Apiretal?
text:
Con 39 de fiebre, lo que importa es el malestar del niño, no el número: el objetivo es su confort, según la SEUP [1]. El paracetamol y el ibuprofeno sirven para bajar la temperatura y mejorar el estado general, a la dosis que indique su pediatra, cada 6-8 horas [1]. No alternes los dos antitérmicos de forma sistemática cada 3-4 horas [1]. La fiebre suele durar entre 2 y 4 días, y que no baje del todo tras el antitérmico es frecuente y no indica más gravedad [4]. Ofrécele líquidos abundantes y no lo fuerces a comer [1].

Consulta si está decaído o muy irritable, le cuesta respirar, tiene manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas o no tolera líquidos [7].

q: mi bebe tiene muchos mocos y le cuesta dormir
text:
Los mocos y la tos son los síntomas típicos del catarro de vías altas, una infección vírica muy frecuente en los primeros años, según la SEUP [3]. La mucosidad puede durar hasta una semana, y la tos incluso más [4].

Para ayudar a dormir, se pueden hacer lavados nasales antes de las tomas y de dormir, preferiblemente con suero salino y nunca con agua del grifo [4]. Conviene ofrecerle abundantes líquidos y mantenerlo alejado del humo [4]. No uses mucolíticos, descongestivos ni jarabes para la tos, sobre todo si es menor de 6 años [4].

Consulta a tu pediatra si le cuesta respirar, respira más deprisa de lo normal, está irritable o le cuesta comer [5].

q: puedo darle Apiretal despues de las vacunas
text: No, no hay ningún problema en darle Apiretal después de las vacunas. Los lactantes que fueron prematuros menores de 28 semanas y pesaron menos de 1500 g tienen mayor riesgo de apnea y bradicardia en las 48-72 horas después de la vacunación, pero son fenómenos transitorios, según la AEP [4]. En los grandes prematuros (menos de 32 semanas) vacunados mientras siguen ingresados se recomienda monitorización cardiorrespiratoria durante esas 72 horas [4]. La dosis de Apiretal depende del peso del niño; puedes calcularla con el dosificador de PediBot.
sources: [4] CAV-AEP — "10. Inmunizaciones en niños prematuros y recién nacidos de riesgo", section

q: mi hijo tiene tos pero no le cuesta respirar
text:
La tos sin dificultad para respirar es lo habitual en un catarro de vías altas, una infección vírica de nariz y garganta muy frecuente en los primeros años, según la SEUP [6]. Es normal que tengan entre 6 y 8 catarros al año, incluso más si va a la guardería [6]. Si además tiene mocos, estornudos o algo de fiebre, encaja con ese cuadro [6].

Conviene vigilar en casa la respiración: si respira más deprisa, se le marcan las costillas, se le hunde el pecho o tiene fatiga al caminar o correr, hay que consultar [2]. También si está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable [2].

text: No mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más es un signo de deshidratación en bebés y niños pequeños, según MedlinePlus [4]. Otros signos son la sequedad de boca y lengua, llorar sin lágrimas, tener sueño o somnolencia inusual, irritabilidad y ojos que parecen hundidos [4]. La amenaza más grave de las enfermedades diarreicas es la deshidratación, según la OMS [5]. Lo más importante es evitarla ofreciendo soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas, sin usar soluciones caseras ni refrescos [3]. Si el bebé tiene mucha sed, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco o tiene los ojos hundidos, hay que consultar [3].

q: mi bebe tiene diarrea desde ayer y hace puro aguado
text:
La diarrea líquida y frecuente es un síntoma típico de la gastroenteritis aguda, según la SEUP [3]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación ofreciendo solución de rehidratación oral en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, después de cada deposición líquida [3]. Los niños deben seguir comiendo, en cantidades pequeñas y frecuentes, y mantener la lactancia si la toma [7].

Consulta cuanto antes si tu bebé tiene menos de un año, o si notas sed intensa, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco o tiene los ojos hundidos [1][2].

q: mi hija tiene salpullido y fiebre pero esta jugando
text:
La fiebre es una señal de que el cuerpo está combatiendo una infección, y no es sinónimo de gravedad, según la SEUP [4]. Lo más habitual es que dure entre 2 y 4 días, aunque puede durar más sin que eso sea motivo de mayor preocupación [2]. Que esté jugando es buena señal: lo importante es vigilar su estado general y que tenga buen color [2]. Ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia y no la fuerces a comer si no tiene apetito [3]. No la bañes en agua fría ni le pongas paños húmedos, porque resulta desagradable y no es eficaz [3]. Consulta a tu pediatra si aparecen puntos rojos en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlos, o si la ves decaída o con mal color [2].

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: mi niño de 4 años tiene ronchas rojas en todo el cuerpo y le dan mucha comezon
text:
Las ronchas rojas que pican mucho son urticaria, y en la infancia la mayoría están ocasionadas por una infección, según la SEUP [1]. Son placas rojas y elevadas que van cambiando de sitio: aparecen en una zona y desaparecen de otras [1]. La urticaria es muy común y suele desaparecer por sí sola, según MedlinePlus [3].

En casa, evite frotar la piel y los baños con agua muy caliente, y no le aplique pomadas ni le dé jarabes sin consultar con su pediatra [2]. Puede comer su comida habitual, sin introducir alimentos nuevos [2].

Consulte en urgencias si respira con dificultad o se le oyen pitos, si no puede tragar o babea mucho, o si se le hincha la cara [4].

q: que hago si mi hijo tiene una convulsion por fiebre
text:
Durante una convulsión febril, tumba al niño de lado en un sitio seguro, lejos de objetos con los que pueda golpearse, y no le introduzcas nada en la boca, según la SEUP [3]. Si puedes, fíjate en cómo se mueve y cuánto dura [3]. Cuando termine, suele quedarse dormido o confuso un rato corto; la convulsión normalmente dura menos de 5 minutos [3]. Si no le has dado antitérmico en las últimas 2 horas, puedes darle paracetamol o ibuprofeno [3].

Consulta en urgencias si es su primera convulsión, si se repite, si lo ves muy dormido, confuso o irritable, o si tiene dolor de cabeza intenso o vómitos repetidos [3].

q: mi hija vomito 4 veces y no quiere tomar suero
text:
Lo prioritario es asegurar el aporte de líquidos para evitar la deshidratación, según la SEUP [6]. Cuando vomite, espera 20 minutos y luego ofrécele suero de rehidratación oral en pequeñas cantidades, 2-5 ml cada 5 minutos durante una hora [6]. Si lo tolera bien, puedes aumentar la frecuencia poco a poco [6]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales [6].

Consulta a tu pediatra si está decaída, vomita muchas veces o no toma líquidos [1]. También si vomita mucho y no tolera sólidos ni líquidos, si los vómitos son verdosos o con sangre, o si está adormilada, tiene mucha sed, los ojos hundidos, llora sin lágrimas u orina poco [7].

q: cuando se empiezan a dar alimentos al bebe
text:
Alrededor de los 6 meses, según MedlinePlus [1]. La leche materna o la fórmula cubren todas sus necesidades hasta entonces [1]. Conviene empezar con un alimento a la vez para poder identificar a cuáles podría ser alérgico [1].

Antes del cuarto mes no se deben introducir alimentos distintos de la leche materna o la fórmula, según la AEP [4]. A partir de esa edad, el momento se individualiza con el pediatra [4].

No le dé miel antes del año, ni leche de vaca antes del año, ni alimentos que puedan provocar asfixia (dulces, palomitas, frutos secos enteros, uvas sin cortar) antes de los 3 años [1].

q: mi bebe tiene la nariz tapada y no puede tomar tetero
text: La nariz tapada es un síntoma habitual del resfrío común, según MedlinePlus [1]. Para un bebé, la leche materna o la fórmula siguen siendo su alimento y su hidratación [3]; ofrécele el tetero con más frecuencia y en menos cantidad, y si le cuesta respirar mientras come, prueba a limpiarle la nariz antes. La deshidratación se previene tomando suficientes líquidos, y cuando el bebé está enfermo conviene darle líquidos adicionales [2]. Consulta a tu doctor si el bebé deja de mojar pañales, está muy somnoliento o rechaza por completo el tetero [2].

La fiebre es una temperatura corporal por encima de 38 ºC y suele indicar que el cuerpo se está defendiendo de una infección, según la SEUP [2]. Lo más habitual es que dure entre 2 y 4 días, y que no baje del todo con un antitérmico no significa que sea más grave [3].

En casa, lo importante es el confort del bebé: ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia, no lo sobreabrigues y no lo bañes en agua fría ni le pongas paños húmedos [4]. q: como saber si mi hijo esta deshidratado
text:
Los signos de deshidratación que conviene vigilar son: mucha sed, llorar sin lágrimas, orinar poco y tener los ojos hundidos, según la SEUP [3]. También puede aparecer irritabilidad marcada, somnolencia o disminución de la capacidad de respuesta [3]. El peligro de deshidratación es mayor cuanto más pequeño es el niño [3].

Para prevenirla, lo prioritario es asegurar el aporte de líquidos, y cuando vomite se recomienda esperar 20 minutos y luego dar suero de rehidratación oral en pequeñas cantidades y tomas frecuentes [6][4]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales [6].

Consulta con tu pediatra si está decaído, vomita muchas veces o no toma líquidos [1].

q: mi nene de 3 años ronca mucho y le cuesta respirar cuando duerme
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 911 / 107 (SAME) o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text:
El ronquido fuerte en un niño de 3 años puede deberse a que la lengua, la boca, la garganta o las vías respiratorias de la nariz vibran y se estrechan al dormir, según el NHS [6]. Cuando además la respiración se detiene y vuelve a empezar, o hay ruidos de jadeo, resoplido o atragantamiento mientras duerme, puede tratarse de apnea del sueño, que necesita tratamiento porque puede causar problemas más serios [7]. Otros signos son despertarse muchas veces, ronquido fuerte y, durante el día, mucho cansancio, dificultad para concentrarse, cambios de humor o dolor de cabeza al despertar [7].

Conviene que un médico lo valore: la apnea del sueño puede ser seria si no se diagnostica ni se trata [7].

q: mi hijo de 12 años se doblo el tobillo jugando al futbol y lo tiene morado
text:
Puede tratarse de un esguince: el tobillo se hincha o se amorata y duele al apoyarlo, según el NHS [1]. Durante los primeros 2 o 3 días sigue la terapia PRICE: protege la zona, reposo sin apoyar el pie, hielo envuelto en un paño hasta 20 minutos cada 2 o 3 horas, un vendaje de compresión y el tobillo elevado [6]. Evita el calor, el alcohol y los masajes esos primeros días [6]. No sigas jugando ni usando la parte dolorida, y no ignores el dolor ni la hinchazón, según MedlinePlus [4].

Acude a urgencias si oíste un crujido al lesionarse, el tobillo cambió de forma o está en ángulo raro, está dormido u hormiguea, o la piel se ve azul o gris o fría al tacto [7]. Consulta también si hay mucho dolor o mucha hinchazón o moretón, o si no mejora tras tratarlo en casa [3].

q: mi bebe tiene pocos pañales mojados hoy
text:
No mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más es un signo de deshidratación en bebés y niños pequeños, según MedlinePlus [2]. Otros signos son la boca y la lengua secas, llorar sin lágrimas, somnolencia o irritabilidad inusual, y los ojos hundidos [2]. La deshidratación puede ser leve o grave, y el peligro es mayor cuanto más pequeño es el niño, según la SEUP [3]. Ofrecer soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas, en pequeñas cantidades y a menudo, es lo más importante para evitarla [3].

Consulta pronto a tu doctor si tu bebé no moja el pañal en 3 horas o más, llora sin lágrimas, está muy irritable o somnoliento, o rechaza beber [2][3].

q: mi hijo tiene manchas rojas despues de la fiebre
text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

Después de la fiebre es frecuente que aparezcan manchas rojas en la piel, y lo importante es comprobar si desaparecen al presionar. Según la SEUP, hay que vigilar la aparición de petequias, que son puntos rojos que no desaparecen al apretar en sus laterales [1]. La prueba del vaso consiste en poner un vaso transparente encima de la mancha y apretar: si no desaparece, son petequias [6].

Consulta sin demora si las manchas no se aclaran al presionarlas, si el niño está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, o si le cuesta respirar [2].

q: wie erkenne ich Austrocknung bei meinem Kind
text:
Bei Austrocknung ersetzt man die verlorenen Flüssigkeiten und Elektrolyte, laut MedlinePlus [1]. Bei leichten Fällen reicht oft viel Wasser; bei Kindern gibt es orale Rehydrationslösungen, die man ohne Rezept kaufen kann [1]. Warnzeichen, bei denen Sie ärztlichen Rat suchen sollten: dunkler, übel riechender Urin oder selteneres Wasserlassen als sonst, laut NHS [3]. Wenn Sie glauben, dass Ihr Kind stark ausgetrocknet ist, rufen Sie Ihren Arzt an [4].

Bei Jugendlichen und vielen geimpften Kindern verläuft Keuchhusten oft nur als lang dauernder Husten ohne die klassischen Begleiterscheinungen [1]. q: mein Baby hat rote Flecken am Bauch und kratzt sich
text: Rote, leicht erhabene Flecken mit Juckreiz und Kribbeln können ein Hitzepickel sein; es kann überall am Körper auftreten und sich ausbreiten, ist aber nicht ansteckend [3]. Am wichtigsten ist, die Haut kühl zu halten: lockere Baumwollkleidung, leichte Bettwäsche, kühle Bäder und ausreichend Flüssigkeit [3]. Gegen den Juckreiz hilft etwas Kaltes, etwa ein feuchtes Tuch oder ein in ein Geschirrtuch gewickeltes Kühlpack, bis zu 20 Minuten; besser tupfen oder klopfen statt kratzen [3]. Verwenden Sie keine parfümierten Duschgele oder Cremes [3]. Bessert es sich nach einigen Tagen nicht oder sind Sie unsicher, lassen Sie es von Ihrer Ärztin oder Ihrem Arzt ansehen [4].

q: mein Kind hat Fieber nach der Impfung
text:
Wenn Ihr Kind jünger als 3 Monate ist, muss Fieber noch am selben Tag ärztlich abgeklärt werden [2].

Bei älteren Kindern ist Fieber nach einer Impfung nichts Ungewöhnliches: Impfungen gehören zu den möglichen Auslösern erhöhter Temperatur [2]. Fieber ist keine Krankheit, sondern meist ein Zeichen dafür, dass der Körper eine Infektion oder Impfung verarbeitet [3]. Die Temperatur wird in der Regel innerhalb von 1 bis 4 Tagen wieder normal [1]. Geben Sie kein Aspirin an Kinder unter 16 Jahren [2]. Die Dosis von Fiebermitteln hängt vom Alter und Gewicht ab; fragen Sie dazu Ihre Ärztin oder Ihren Arzt.

Suchen Sie ärztliche Hilfe, wenn Ihr Kind unter 3 Monaten 38 °C oder mehr hat, 3 bis 6 Monate alt ist und 39 °C oder mehr hat, einen Hautausschlag zeigt, das Fieber 5 Tage oder länger anhält, nicht trinken will oder dehydriert wirkt [2].

Bei Erbrechen ohne Durchfall kann sich die Erkrankung auf das Erbrechen beschränken; meist dauern die Beschwerden etwa 12 bis 48 Stunden, so das RKI [1]. Achten Sie darauf, dass Ihr Kind ausreichend trinkt, damit kein Flüssigkeitsmangel entsteht [1]. Kinder unter 6 Jahren mit einer infektiösen Magen-Darm-Erkrankung dürfen Gemeinschaftseinrichtungen erst 48 Stunden nach Abklingen der Symptome wieder besuchen [4]. Wenden Sie sich an Ihren Arzt, wenn Ihr Kind nicht trinken kann, weniger Urin absetzt oder sehr schlapp wirkt [1].

Hinweis: 10 kg ist für 4 Jahre laut den WHO-Wachstumskurven sehr wenig. Wenn das Gewicht stimmt, lassen Sie das Wachstum bald in der Kinderarztpraxis prüfen; wenn es ein Tippfehler war, korrigieren Sie ihn, denn Dosierungen richten sich nach dem Gewicht.

q: Was sind Zeichen von Austrocknung? (Alter: 4 Jahre) (Gewicht: 10 kg)
text:
Bei Austrocknung durch Erbrechen sind die Warnzeichen zum Beispiel dunkler, stark riechender Urin oder weniger Urin als sonst, so der NHS [3]. Auch wenn Ihr Kind nicht trinken kann oder sehr schlapp wirkt, sollten Sie ärztlichen Rat suchen [1]. Bei leichter Austrocknung reicht oft, viel Wasser zu trinken; bei Kindern geben Sie eine orale Rehydratationslösung, die Sie ohne Rezept bekommen [1][6]. Bei schwerer Austrocknung kann eine Behandlung mit Flüssigkeit über die Vene im Krankenhaus nötig sein [1][4].

Hinweis: 10 kg ist für 4 Jahre laut den WHO-Wachstumskurven sehr wenig. Wenn das Gewicht stimmt, lassen Sie das Wachstum bald in der Kinderarztpraxis prüfen; wenn es ein Tippfehler war, korrigieren Sie ihn, denn Dosierungen richten sich nach dem Gewicht.

q: mein 2-jähriges kind hat bellenden husten in der nacht
text:
Ein bellender Husten, der nachts schlimmer wird, spricht bei einem Kleinkind am ehesten für einen Pseudokrupp (Krupp), so das NHS [1]. Typisch sind außerdem eine heisere Stimme und ein pfeifendes, rasselndes Geräusch beim Einatmen, oft nach ein paar Tagen mit Erkältungssymptomen [1]. Krupp wird meist durch Viren ausgelöst, beginnt wie eine Erkältung und bessert sich in der Regel nach drei bis fünf Tagen [4]. Die meisten Fälle sind mild und können zu Hause behandelt werden [4].

Wichtig: Ihr Kind nicht in einen dampfigen Raum bringen und keinen Dampf einatmen lassen [7]. Suchen Sie sofort ärztliche Hilfe, wenn Ihr Kind schwer atmet, sich die Rippen beim Atmen einziehen, die Haut bläulich oder blass wird, sehr schläfrig oder schwer zu wecken ist oder nicht mehr normal reagiert [7].
